Description: A Jewish town and revolt fortress on a camel-shaped ridge in the Golan, excavated by Shmarya Gutman. It holds one of the earliest known synagogues, built before AD 70, and fell to the Romans in AD 67 after a siege described by Josephus. Gamla is not named in the Bible; its value is the world it reveals.
BiblicalSignificance: Gamla's synagogue shows what worship looked like in Jesus' lifetime: a plain hall where the law was read to a gathered town, without a Temple and without a priesthood. It is the ordinary religious life behind the Gospels' synagogue scenes, preserved in stone.
Interpretations: Scholars agree Gamla is a 1st-century Jewish town with an early synagogue; debate concerns details of the siege narrative in Josephus, not the town's identity or its synagogue.
